title: Ashur-nadin-shumi made king of Babylon
summary: Sennacherib puts his son Ashur-nadin-shumi on the throne of Babylon.
description: Sennacherib puts his son Ashur-nadin-shumi on the throne of Babylon. Event record added from Griffith & White’s Reply to Beckman, Part 2 (Table 3, row 700, pp. 45–46; Table 2, row 700, p. 42).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH Reply to Beckman (Griffith & White, Part 2): 700 BC (Sennacherib year 5).

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 2: An Objectivist Answer to the Assyrian Synchronisms," OSF preprint v2.10 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/DT6GX, Table 3, row 700, pp. 45–46; Table 2, row 700, p. 42
chronologies.note: Sennacherib sacks Babylon in Bel-Ibni’s third year and makes his son king; last battle against Merodach-Baladan, who escapes again.
